nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: responseMode is explicitly responseNode (reference lesson: unset means an instant 'Workflow was started'). Set allowedOrigins to the Netlify URL.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Set SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY after import.

nodes.name: Auth: read token
nodes.notes: Uses .first() on Webhook - singleton upstream node, so no paired-item ambiguity.

nodes.name: Auth: verify token
nodes.notes: Auth check block 2/4. Supabase Auth validates the JWT (signature, expiry). neverError + fullResponse so a 401 is data for 'Auth: check role', not a crash.

nodes.name: Auth: load profile
nodes.notes: Auth check block 3/4. Reads profiles with the service role. If the token was invalid it asks for the all-zero id, which matches nothing, and 'Auth: check role' has already got the 401 from the previous node.

nodes.name: Auth: check role
nodes.notes: Every downstream node reads the caller from $('Auth: check role').first().json.user - never from the request body. client_viewer workflows must also check user.client_id against the requested resource.

nodes.name: Respond: denied
nodes.notes: Same deny node in every webhook workflow. Returns 401/403/500 with a plain message; never echoes the token or profile.

nodes.name: Get Google Ads secrets
nodes.notes: Developer token, OAuth client id/secret, refresh token and MCC id, entered by Rob on the dashboard Settings page (stored in Supabase private.google_ads_secrets - never readable by the browser).

nodes.name: Refresh Google token
nodes.notes: OAuth refresh, same as the reference. Values from 'Get Google Ads secrets'. Test: Execute step - the output must contain access_token.

nodes.name: Suggest locations

parameters.jsonHeaders: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ "Authorization": "Bearer " + ($('Refresh Google token').first().json.access_token || 'missing'), "developer-token": $('Get Google Ads secrets').first().json.developer_token || '', "Content-Type": "application/json" }, null ? { "login-customer-id": null } : {})) }}
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ locationNames: { names: [$('Validate input').first().json.query] }, locale: 'en' }, $('Validate input').first().json.country ? { countryCode: $('Validate input').first().json.country } : {})) }}

nodes.notes: geoTargetConstants:suggest is global - no customer id and no login-customer-id.
